title: Airflow-style batch orchestration
subtitle: A portable task graph over real data
description: Use the shared DAG runner for extraction, SQL cleaning and aggregation. The advanced Airflow simulator source is retained for migration; Python DAG authoring is not executed by this root yet.

steps.title: Copy source orders into Bronze
steps.concept: Copy moves records; it does not clean them. A stored procedure belongs to the source database, not to Data Factory.
steps.task: Retain all 12 source orders, including the negative and zero amounts.
steps.hint: Keep Bronze unchanged. Cleaning belongs in Silver.

check.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM bronze.orders

steps.title: Clean orders as a SQL task
steps.concept: The orchestrator schedules a task; SQL performs the transformation.
steps.task: Clean orders as a SQL task

check.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(net_amount) AS revenue FROM silver.orders

steps.title: Aggregate the scheduled batch
steps.code: SELECT customer_id, SUM(net_amount) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM silver.orders GROUP BY customer_id
steps.solution: SELECT customer_id, SUM(net_amount) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM silver.orders GROUP BY customer_id
steps.concept: The root executes dependency-ordered tasks and records actual task outcomes. It is not an Apache Airflow scheduler.

check.sql: SELECT customer_id, revenue, orders FROM gold.customer_revenue ORDER BY customer_id
